title: Release v0.7.1
Set the default version of runtime to 2.1 and Python to 3.7
description:
The default version 1.9 of the runtime [ended its availability](https://cloud.google.com/ai-platform/training/docs/runtime-version-list) on March 16, 2020. Therefore, the default version of the runtime is set to 2.1, which requires to be used in conjunction with Python 3.7. 

In line 40 of `deploy.py`, the function `sys.stdout.write()` throws an error (`write()` argument must be `str`, not `bytes`), when it is executed under Python 3.7 (instead of Python 2.7). The `line`  should be decoded into `str` using `utf-8` encoding.

title: Adds basic deployment use to deployment vignette
description:
You can host your trained machine learning models in the cloud using the Cloud ML
prediction service to infer target values for new data. This can improve performance
and make your models easily available for others to consume. 

## Exporting a SavedModel

The Cloud ML prediction service makes use of models exported through the
`export_savedmodel()` function which is available for the `tensorflow`, `keras` and
`tfestimators` packages or any other tool that support the [tf.train.Saver](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/train/Saver) interface.

For instance, we can define and export a simple model by running:

```r
library(tensorflow)
library(cloudml)

# define output folder
model_dir <- tempfile()

# define simple string-based tensor operations
sess <- tf$Session()
name <- tf$placeholder(tf$string)
hello <- tf$string_join(inputs = c("Hello, ", name, "!"))

# export as a savedmodel
export_savedmodel(
  sess,
  model_dir,
  inputs = list(name = name),
  outputs = list(hello = hello))
```

```
[1] "/var/folders/fz/v6wfsg2x1fb1rw4f6r0x4jwm0000gn/T//Rtmp9OCDeo/filee7ef3e841204/saved_model.pb"
```

## Deployment

Deployment is performed through `cloudml_deploy()` which uses the same `gcloud`
and `cloudml` configuration concepts used while training. We can
train any exported model by running:

```r
cloudml_deploy(model_dir)
```
```
Model created and available in https://console.cloud.google.com/mlengine/models/cloudml
```

Notice that models make use of unique names and versions which can be specified
using the `name` and `version` parameters in `cloudml_deploy()`.

## Prediction

Once a model is deployed, predictions can be performed by providing a list of inputs into
`cloudml_predict()`:

```r
cloudml_predict(
  list(
    list(name = "cloudml"),
    list(name = "tensorflow")
  )
)
```

```
$predictions
               hello
1    Hello, cloudml!
2 Hello, tensorflow!
```

Similar to `cloudml_deploy()`, `cloudml_predict()` makes use of the same configuration
concepts and `name` and `version` parameters.

For additional settings and resources visit [Google Cloud Platform - Prediction Basics](https://cloud.google.com/ml-engine/docs/prediction-overview)

title: support for training flags
description:
As of now training flags don't work due to tfruns barfing on the `--job-dir` parameter. I am attempting to get this working again. Step 1 is this change to tfruns:

https://github.com/rstudio/tfruns/commit/8d79cda94d93f4c47887e46e1992d48f756a6342

The next piece is actually inserting `--args` in the call to Rscript so `--job-dir` is ignored:

https://github.com/rstudio/cloudml/commit/26328cc6bc09983a8cf5f2c00777617a38c1bf31#diff-58c56482f1d1f4e82fca67ca753b91fa

The other piece of this PR is eliminating the use of `...` in the signature of `cloudml_train` and substituting an explicit `flags` parameter. This provides both syntactic compatibility with `tfruns::training_run` as well as adds support for passing a YAML file with the flags rather than requiring them to specified inline.

This also makes `cloudml_tune()` largely the same function as `cloudml_train()` (as both now sport a `hypertune` parameter). I still think it's worthwhile to have 2 functions though as the `cloudml_tune()` version *requires* the `hypertune` parameter and also provides top-level visibility into hyperparmeter tuning.

title: Caching, packrat and travis improvements
description: There is already support for caching r packages, but similar improvements could be used to lower training time while using keras datasets and python packages. Completed work: - Support for caching pip packages, currently disabled **[reverted]** - Support to cache packrat appropriately and example. - Support to cache keras data dir. - Support to test multiple config files in travis. - Support disabling keras installation and upgrading r to allow fast startup times. The big improvement in performance is the work to enable packrat for keras while maintaining descent execution times: Python package caching was reverted since it showed a performance degradation rather than an improvement. This is, most likely, explained by further optimizations in cloudml to which invalidating the state of the `sitepackages()` triggers further work that offsets the improvements of caching.

title: Improve training time performance
description: Took a closer look at the ~3min training time: ~ 45s: Upgrade all System Packages ~ 30s: Install R System Dependencies ~ 45s: Upgrade TensorFlow ~ 10s: Initialize Python ~ 10s: Restore R packages from cache ~ 5s: Download train examples, train, upload results ~ 40s: Tearing down TensorFlow. This PR proposes removing the following stages: ~ 45s: Upgrade all System Packages ~ 45s: Upgrade TensorFlow Upgrading TensorFlow to use tfestimators uncovered a hang in both Python and R that CloudML needs to resolve. Upgrading all system packages shouldn't be required in most cases since we can rely on CloudML image having a recent version. to

title: Improve README and pckdown site
Add cloudml tests and travis integration
description: Adds tests and Travis integration using cloudml to catch early breaking changes.

title: Add packages cache and other train improvements
description: The are 3 changes in this PR: **1. Add support for caching packages.** Caching is enabled by default and is based on the `storage` field under `cloudml.yml`, a cache can be shared across configurations by specifying a storage path under `cache` or disabled by setting `cache` to `FALSE`. **2. Enable packrat.** Packrat is now enabled by default to create a definition file with a list of packages and versions which then becomes part of the cloudml deployment to restore the packages. This can be disabled by setting `packrat` to `FALSE` under `cloudml.yml`. **3. Use RStudio terminal for cloudml_train logs** This change makes use of the RStudio terminal, if available, to stream the logs and finally download the job run once the job completes. Additional changes: - Renames a few SDK functions: - gcloud to gcloud_path - gsutil to gsutil_path - gs_copy to gsutil_copy - gs_data to gsutil_data - Adds a few "for internal use" sdk functions. - Use `processx` instead of `system2`. - Refactors examples to be under `inst`. - Adds examples for `mtcars` (Python and R) and `mnist` - Changes README to use `mnist` to avoid using `tfestimators` until TF 1.3 becomes supported in cloudml. - Adds support to use reference in GitHub repos. - Fix to retrieve job results after training.

title: WIP: Implement a variety of Google SDK methods
description:
Implement/refactor a variety of Google SDK methods, mostly as a way to get the README working for a different account and without using the `gcloud` binary from the terminal:

- sdk_install: Installs the Google SDK, currently OS X only.
- gcloud_config: Reads the Google SDK config.
- gcloud_exec: Executes a Google SDK command.
- gcloud_login: Login to Google SDK.
- gcloud_path: Finds Google SDK path.

title: cross platform implementation of copy_directory
description:
@kevinushey This appears to work fine for cross platform recursive file copying. We basically apply the include and exclude filters (which are defined using glob syntax) to the top level listing of files and then copy each of those top level items recursively into the target directory. 

FWIW this is the same code that I've been using in R Markdown websites.

title: refactoring around overlay construction
description: This PR seeks to clean up how the overlay (runtime configuration) is constructed -- effectively making the process somewhat more declarative, and also adding support for `job_output` and `job_name` in the process.

title: improve handling + construction of shell arguments
description:
This PR does a few things:

1. Fixes the handling of potentially nested lists-of-lists when passed to a shell arguments builder,
2. Ensures that alternate format characters (e.g. `%i`) are handled,
3. Implicitly discards any inputs containing `NULL`s (making it easier to just pass through potentially missing arguments, cleaning up a few call sites)

title: use 'cloudml' prefix for command line arguments we own
description: This PR standardizes the names of the command line arguments we pass a little bit, and uses the `parse_arguments()` API to read + handle them.

title: Introduce config function
description:
This PR introduces a `cloudml::config` function which takes care of a few things:

1. Providing defaults and auto-generating config values (we'll need this for smart `job_dir` creation)

2. Optional automatic download of `gs://` URLs

3. Enforcing the use of `config.yml` (we rely on this elsewhere)

title: Filter for custom config values
description:
Could be passed either from ... of train_local / train_cloud or via hyperparemters provided on the command line by cloudml

Note that I didn't yet implement the behavior for `train_local` because I wasn't sure how it differed from `train_cloud`.

Also note that command line forwarding of hyper-parameters is marked as a TODO.

title: use a config-driven approach to training
description: This PR attempts to port the `census` example to a config-driven approach to modeling.
